text: When developers work with APIs, they send HTTP requests to a server to get or send data. Most APIs return responses in JSON, a simple format that both humans and computers can read. Before making requests, you usually need authentication, such as an API key, to prove who you are. Once you have access, you still need to be careful about rate limits, which control how many requests you can make in a certain time. If you send too many, the server may block you temporarily. Finally, good error handling is essential. This means checking the HTTP status code and response body so you can fix problems or retry when something goes wrong, making your code much more reliable.
